newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen weaker on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen weaker on mild weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open lower Friday on forecasts of mild weather through the West in early August, industry sources said.
"Things are dipping a little bit," said one futures trader.

In early over the counter activity, September Palo Verde (PV) was said to have traded at $28.10 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from Thursday's NYMEX futures close at $28.63 per MWh. Support for September PV was seen at $28.00 per MWh.
September California Oregon Border (COB) was also expected to open lower, although sources said COB over the counter business was thin early Friday.
Both the PV and COB contracts eased Thursday amidst the mild weather forecast and relatively strong generation in the West.

In generation news as of early Friday, the 700 megawatt (MW) turbine 23 at the massive Grand Coulee hydropower dam in Washington state was taken off line early Thursday for scheduled repair work through the remainder of the year.
Meanwhile, the dam's 700 MW turbine 24 was returned to service Thursday after being taken off line earlier in the week for unplanned repairs.
In addition, Grand Coulee's 600 MW turbine 21 is scheduled to resume operations later Thursday, completing a scheduled maintenance and repair outage which began in February.
Outflows from Grand Coulee, which has a total rated capacity of 6,150 MW, have to tapered off this week amid re-filling of the reservoir ahead of August fish flow requirements.
The 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power complex in New Mexico was expected to restart Sunday after being shut earlier this month for repairs.
The 254 MW unit 1 at the Valmy coal-fired power plant in Nevada was expected to restart Sunday or Monday after being shut earlier this week due to a rotor problem.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to be near-normal over the weekend and then cooling to one to five degrees Fahrenheit below normal by the end of the weekend and into early next week, Weather Services Corp said.
In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be near-normal into early next week, with possible temperatures slightly below normal in the south.
Transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie, which links the Pacific Northwest to Southern Califoria, remained at 6,300 MW pending final approval of system operating procedures.
Once those are cleared, which is expected to happen by Monday, the rating will be lifted to 6,900 MW.
